column1: # Concurrency functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Runs a procedure alongside the program, copying its arguments at that moment.
Holds a typed queue between goroutines; copies share it, and a new one is nil.
Returns the buffer size the channel was made with; 0 means each value is handed over.
Returns true for a default-constructed channel, which blocks forever if used.
Sends a value, waiting for room or a receiver; raises an error if the channel is closed.
Receives a value, waiting for one; returns false once closed and drained.
Sends a value only if it can go at once; returns false if it would have to wait.
Receives a value only if one is ready; returns false if empty or closed.
Sends a value, waiting at most ms milliseconds; returns false on a timeout.
Receives a value, waiting at most ms milliseconds; false on a timeout or end of stream.
Marks that no more values will be sent; values already buffered are still delivered.
Returns true once the channel is closed, even while values are still buffered.
Returns how many values are buffered right now, as a snapshot.
Returns the iterator a for each loop uses to receive until the channel is drained.
Holds a for each loop's place while it receives from a channel.
Holds a send-only view of a channel, for a procedure that only produces.
Holds a receive-only view of a channel, which cannot send to it or close it.
Adds 1, or a given amount, to the work outstanding; call it before the spawn.
Subtracts one from the work outstanding; raises an error if it would go below zero.
Waits until the work outstanding reaches zero.
Waits at most ms milliseconds for the work to reach zero; returns false on a timeout.
Returns how much work is still outstanding, as a snapshot.
Holds the background context, which is never cancelled and is the root of all others.
Returns a child context that you cancel yourself.
Returns a child context that cancels itself after the given milliseconds.
Cancels the context and every context made from it; a second call is harmless.
Returns true once the context is cancelled or its deadline has passed.
Returns why the context ended: "cancelled", "deadline exceeded", or "" while live.
Returns how many goroutines exist right now, as a snapshot for diagnostics.
Returns how many OS threads the scheduler is running goroutines on.
Starts a procedure on a new thread, passing it one pointer; returns the thread handle.
Waits for a thread to finish, then releases its handle.
Releases a thread handle without waiting; the thread runs on to its end.
Returns the handle of the thread that calls it.
Creates a mutex and returns its handle, or 0 on failure.
Locks a mutex, waiting while another thread holds it.
Unlocks a mutex so that a waiting thread can take it.
Destroys a mutex once no thread is using it.
Creates a condition variable and returns its handle, or 0 on failure.
Unlocks the mutex and waits for a signal, then locks the mutex again.
Wakes one thread waiting on the condition; the signal is lost if none is waiting.
Wakes every thread waiting on the condition.
Destroys a condition variable once no thread is waiting on it.
